chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then hasten to the Remembrance of Allah'?' He said: 'Work (do good deeds) and hasten, for it is a busy day for the Muslims, and the reward of the deeds of the Muslims during it is proportional to the busyness imposed upon them, and the good deeds and the sins are multiplied during it.'

He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, it has reached me that the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to prepare for Friday on the day of Thursday, because it is a busy day for the Muslims.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Friday in Shia Islam and how should Muslims prepare for it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) interprets the Quranic imperative to 'hasten to the Remembrance of Allah' (Surah Al-Jumu'ah) as a call for spiritual urgency, noting that Friday is a day of 'restriction' (mudayyaq) where the weight of deeds is magnified. This hadith highlights the practical tradition of the Prophet's companions, who began preparing for Friday worship on Thursday, underscoring the day's unique status in Shia jurisprudence as a time of intensified reward and accountability.
